name: Normandy landings
note: The plan shows the whole operation of 6 June 1944, not a single field: the blocks are fleets, divisions and airborne forces. The accounts give the sectors in order from west to east (Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno, Sword) but not distances, so the places of the beaches, towns and German units are set by judgement. Pointe du Hoc and the French Resistance's sabotage are left off the plan.

terrain.name: Normandy coast
terrain.quote: The target 80-kilometre (50 mi) stretch of the Normandy coast was divided into five sectors: Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno, and Sword.

terrain.name: Sainte-Mère-Église
terrain.quote: they captured the important crossroads at Sainte-Mère-Église

terrain.name: Carentan
terrain.quote: but Carentan, Saint-Lô, and Bayeux remained in German hands

terrain.name: Bayeux
terrain.quote: Bayeux was not captured the first day because of stiff resistance from the 352nd Infantry Division

terrain.name: Caen
terrain.quote: Caen, a major objective, was still in German hands at the end of D-Day

terrain.name: Pegasus Bridge
terrain.quote: The first Allied action of D-Day was the capture of the Caen canal and Orne river bridges via a glider assault at 00:16

units.name: Allied invasion fleet
units.quote: The invasion fleet, which was drawn from eight different navies, comprised 6,939 vessels

units.name: US 82nd and 101st Airborne
units.quote: Paratroopers of the 82nd and 101st Airborne Divisions, numbering over 13,000 men, were delivered by Douglas C-47 Skytrains

units.name: British 6th Airborne Division
units.quote: The British 6th Airborne Division, on the eastern flank, was assigned to capture intact the bridges over the Caen Canal and River Orne

units.name: US 4th Infantry Division
units.quote: Members of the 8th Infantry Regiment of the 4th Infantry Division were the first to land, arriving at 06:30.

units.name: US 1st and 29th Divisions
units.quote: Omaha, the most heavily defended beach, was assigned to the 1st Infantry Division and 29th Infantry Division.

units.name: British 50th Division
units.quote: The first landings on Gold Beach were set for 07:25 because of the differences in the tide between there and the US beaches.

units.name: 3rd Canadian Division
units.quote: The landing at Juno Beach was delayed because of choppy seas, and the men arrived ahead of their supporting armour

units.name: British 3rd Division
units.quote: On Sword Beach, 21 of 25 DD tanks of the first wave were successful in getting safely ashore to provide cover for the infantry, who began disembarking at 07:30.

units.name: 919th Grenadier Regiment
units.quote: Utah Beach was in the area defended by two battalions of the 919th Grenadier Regiment.

units.name: 352nd Infantry Division
units.quote: They faced the 352nd Infantry Division rather than the expected single regiment.

units.name: 716th Static Infantry Division
units.quote: Allied forces attacking Gold, Juno, and Sword Beaches faced the following German units

phases.title: Airborne troops land behind the beaches
phases.text: Pathfinders of the US airborne divisions arrived at 00:15, and British glider troops took the Caen canal and Orne bridges at 00:16. Many paratroopers landed far from their drop zones.
phases.quote: The US airborne landings began with the arrival of pathfinders at 00:15.

phases.title: The flanks are taken
phases.text: On the western side the 82nd Airborne captured the crossroads at Sainte-Mère-Église within two hours of landing. On the eastern side the 6th Airborne held the bridges over the Caen canal and the Orne.
phases.quote: Both bridges were quickly captured intact, with light casualties by the Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire Light Infantry Regiment.

phases.title: The fleet shells the coast
phases.text: Warships bombarded the ground behind the beaches in the dark and, from 05:50, pre-assigned targets on the beaches themselves. The assault divisions crossed in landing craft, which strong winds blew east of their intended positions.
phases.quote: Naval bombardment of areas behind the beach commenced at 05:45, while it was still dark

phases.title: Utah and Omaha are landed on
phases.text: The 8th Infantry Regiment of the 4th Division landed first at Utah at 06:30, about 1,800 metres south of its intended place. At Omaha, where the 1st and 29th Divisions came ashore, obstacles were largely undamaged and fire from the cliffs was heavy.
phases.quote: Members of the 8th Infantry Regiment of the 4th Infantry Division were the first to land, arriving at 06:30.

phases.title: Gold, Sword and Juno are landed on
phases.text: Landings at Gold were set for 07:25 and infantry began disembarking at Sword at 07:30. At Juno the landing was delayed by choppy seas, and the men arrived ahead of their supporting armour and suffered many casualties.
phases.quote: The first landings on Gold Beach were set for 07:25 because of the differences in the tide between there and the US beaches.

phases.title: Combat teams leave Utah Beach
phases.text: Combat teams began to leave Utah at around 09:00, some infantry wading through flooded fields. They skirmished with the 919th Grenadier Regiment through the day, and the 4th Division made a rendezvous with the airborne troops.
phases.quote: Combat teams began to exit the beach at around 09:00, with some infantry wading through the flooded fields rather than travelling on the single road.

phases.title: Barely 600 men reach the heights at Omaha
phases.text: Exit from Omaha was possible only through five heavily defended gullies, and by late morning barely 600 men had reached the higher ground. By noon the Americans were able to clear some lanes on the beaches.
phases.quote: Exit from the beach was possible only via five heavily defended gullies, and by late morning barely 600 men had reached the higher ground.

phases.title: Fortified towns are cleared at Gold, Juno and Sword
phases.text: At Gold, Juno and Sword the fortified towns were cleared in house-to-house fighting. The 2nd Battalion, King's Shropshire Light Infantry advanced on Caen to within a few kilometres of the town but had to withdraw for lack of armour support.
phases.quote: At Gold, Juno, and Sword, several fortified towns were cleared in house-to-house fighting

phases.title: The 21st Panzer Division counter-attacks
phases.text: The 21st Panzer Division attacked between Sword and Juno and nearly reached the Channel. It met stiff resistance from the British 3rd Division and was soon recalled to the area between Caen and Bayeux.
phases.quote: At 16:00, the 21st Panzer Division mounted a counter-attack between Sword and Juno and nearly succeeded in reaching the Channel.
